2610.08577.title: How Learning Governs Unlearning across the Memorization-Generalization Spectrum
2610.08577.paper_summary: While unlearning seeks to negate undesired capabilities acquired through learning, little research has examined how the way models learn shapes their subsequent unlearning. In this paper, we investigate this connection from the perspectives of memorization and generalization, the two most representative yet competing strategies that models employ during training. We first classify memorization- and generalization-heavy models using grokking in modular addition and compare their responses to unlearning, showing that the latter suffer greater retain damage, i.e., a larger performance drop on the retain set. Furthermore, we conduct a finer-grained analysis by introducing bucketed modular addition, in which the respective contributions of the two strategies can be explicitly controlled across the memorization-generalization spectrum. In this setup, we reaffirm that the same trend persists and is nearly monotonic. We further demonstrate that this relationship also holds in LLM unlearning across verbatim and factual recall settings. Finally, we provide two practical insights for developing better unlearning methods, highlighting the importance of accounting for learning dynamics in unlearning.
2610.08577.paper_summary_zh: 雖然去學習旨在否定通過學習獲得的不良能力，但很少有研究探討模型學習的方式如何影響其後續的去學習。本文從記憶和泛化的角度研究這一聯繫，這是模型在訓練過程中採用的兩種最具代表性但又相互競爭的策略。我們首先使用模組化加法中的理解來分類以記憶和泛化為主的模型，並比較它們對去學習的反應，顯示後者在保留集上遭受更大的保留損害，即性能下降更大。此外，我們通過引入分桶模組化加法進行更細緻的分析，在這種情況下，兩種策略的各自貢獻可以在記憶-泛化光譜上明確控制。在這種設置中，我們重申相同的趨勢持續存在，並且幾乎是單調的。我們進一步證明，這一關係在逐字和事實回憶設置中的大型語言模型去學習中也成立。最後，我們提供了兩個實用的見解，以開發更好的去學習方法，強調考慮學習動態在去學習中的重要性。
